title: Powderfinger are back: where to start before the big top rolls into town
dek: Eighteen shows in a travelling big top from September 2027. Here's the catch-up listening, album by album.
body:
Nobody really expected it. Sixteen years after the farewell shows, all five members of Powderfinger are getting back together for a national tour in a travelling big top, starting at Brisbane Showgrounds in September 2027 and finishing at Melbourne Park Oval at the end of October. Tickets went quickly, and extra shows have already been added.

If you were there the first time, you don't need telling. If you were too young, or you only know the songs from the radio, here's where to start.

Internationalist (1998)

This is where Powderfinger went from a good Brisbane rock band to a national fixture. "The Day You Come" and "Passenger" are the big ones, but the album holds together as a record you play start to finish.

Odyssey Number Five (2000)

The one most people own. "My Happiness" and "These Days" are on it, and so is the reason the band could fill arenas for the next decade. If you only buy one Powderfinger record, make it this one.

Vulture Street (2003)

Louder, rawer and more of a rock record, made by a band that clearly wanted to plug in and turn up. It's a good counterweight to the polish of Odyssey.

Then the rest

Double Allergic (1996) is the sound of the band finding its feet, and Dream Days at the Hotel Existence (2007) and Golden Rule (2009) round out the story. In 2020 the band played the "One Night Lonely" livestream from their own homes and raised money for Support Act and Beyond Blue, a good hint that this reunion was always possible.

The tour runs through Brisbane, Cairns, Perth, Sydney, Adelaide and Melbourne. Full dates are on our tours page.

title: System of a Down and Faith No More: a two-band primer for January
dek: A stadium tour with Faith No More as special guests. Here are the albums to play on the drive in.
body:
System of a Down's first Australian headline tour in over a decade lands in January 2027, with stadium shows in Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane. They're bringing Faith No More along as special guests. That's two of the strangest, most influential heavy bands of the last 35 years on one bill.

System of a Down: the essentials

Toxicity (2001) is the starting point. "Chop Suey!", "Toxicity" and "Aerials" are all here, and the album still sounds like nothing else: frantic, political, funny and heavy all at once.

System of a Down (1998), the debut, is rougher and angrier. Play it next if Toxicity hooks you.

Mezmerize and Hypnotize (2005) came out six months apart as two halves of one project. "B.Y.O.B." and "Lonely Day" are the ones you'll hear the crowd singing.

Steal This Album! (2002) collects songs from the Toxicity era and is better than a leftovers record has any right to be.

Faith No More: don't skip the support

The Real Thing (1989) has "Epic" on it and is the obvious way in. Angel Dust (1992) is the one the fans will tell you about: darker, weirder and the reason so many heavy bands of the '90s sounded the way they did.

Dates and venues are on our tours page.
